text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Incisional biopsy of the lip lesion today, with pathology; sun protection for the lips and skin (lip balm with SPF 30 or higher, a broad-brimmed hat); dental review
  • Otolaryngology (head and neck surgery) consultation for a suspected lip cancer: staging, treatment, management of the neck, and surveillance
  • Secondary prevention for chronic coronary disease: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks after starting and a goal LDL below 55 mg/dL, metoprolol succinate for angina, sublingual nitroglycerin with written instructions, blood pressure below 130/80, an echocardiogram to measure heart function before surgery, and staying tobacco-free
  • Cardiac rehabilitation once the lip wound has healed: up to 36 supervised exercise and education sessions for stable angina, with nutrition, activity, and risk-factor coaching
  • Care organized around his choices: information about Sac and Fox Nation health services and Indian Health Service, tribal, and urban Indian health programs, help to use them if he wishes, and room for any traditional or spiritual practices he chooses; costs and options explained plainly
  • V-excision of the lip cancer under local anesthesia with 5 to 10 mm clinical margins and frozen-section margin control, primary closure; contrast CT of the neck before surgery; no elective neck dissection if the final depth of invasion is small; aspirin and metoprolol continued through surgery
  • Surveillance after lip cancer: history and examination of the lips, mouth and neck every 1 to 3 months in the first year, every 2 to 6 months in the second, every 4 to 8 months in years 3 to 5, then yearly; whole-skin examination; dental care; tobacco-free; imaging only for symptoms or findings
  • Ezetimibe 10 mg daily added to atorvastatin because LDL was 68 mg/dL, above the goal of 55 mg/dL, with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks later

resource.title: Jim Thorpe synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care for a 63-year-old Sac and Fox man, a former Olympic and professional athlete, with a non-healing lower-lip lesion and chronic coronary disease: biopsy of a suspicious lip lesion, squamous cell carcinoma of the lip staged and treated by excision with clear margins, sun and tobacco exposure history, surveillance and second-primary prevention on the NCCN head and neck guideline; perioperative cardiac assessment for low-risk surgery with aspirin continued; secondary prevention after a heart attack (aspirin, a high-intensity statin with ezetimibe to the LDL goal, a beta-blocker for angina, blood pressure) and cardiac rehabilitation on the 2023 AHA/ACC chronic coronary disease guideline and the CMID ischemic heart disease monograph; and care options offered with respect, including coordination with Sac and Fox Nation or Indian Health Service programs, without assuming his preferences.
